sentence: She brought up an interesting topic at the meeting
explanation: 'Bring up' significa mencionar. Pasado: 'brought up'. Es separable: 'brought an interesting topic up' también es correcto.

sentence: We need to check in at the hotel before noon
explanation: 'Check in' significa registrarse en un hotel. 'Need to' va seguido de la forma base.

sentence: He found out the truth about the accident yesterday
hint: Past tense of 'find out' is 'found out'
explanation: 'Find out' significa descubrir. Pasado: 'found out' (irregular). 'Finded' no existe.

sentence: They get along very well with their neighbours
explanation: 'Get along' significa tener una buena relación. Con 'they' se usa 'get', no 'gets'.

sentence: I have already filled in the application form
hint: Present perfect: have + already + past participle
explanation: 'Fill in' significa completar un formulario. Es separable: 'filled the application form in' también es correcto.

sentence: She gave up smoking two years ago
hint: Past tense of 'give up' is 'gave up'
explanation: 'Give up' significa dejar de hacer algo. Pasado: 'gave up' (irregular).

sentence: Can you look after the children this afternoon
explanation: 'Look after' significa cuidar de. Las preguntas con 'can' empiezan con el modal.

sentence: He ran into his old friend at the supermarket
explanation: 'Run into' significa encontrarse con alguien por casualidad. Pasado: 'ran into' (irregular). 'Runned' no existe.

sentence: We have to clean up the kitchen after dinner
hint: have to + base form of phrasal verb
explanation: 'Clean up' significa ordenar. Es separable: 'clean the kitchen up' también es correcto.

sentence: They carried on working until midnight last Friday
explanation: 'Carry on' significa continuar. Pasado: 'carried on' (regular, y→ied). 'Carryed' es incorrecto.

sentence: We had to put off the meeting until next week
hint: Subject + had to + phrasal verb + object + time expression
explanation: 'Put off' significa posponer. Es separable: 'put the meeting off' también es correcto.

sentence: She turned up late for the interview again
hint: Subject + phrasal verb + adverb + prepositional phrase
explanation: 'Turn up' significa llegar a algún lugar, a menudo de forma inesperada o tarde.

sentence: He did not show up for the party last night
hint: Subject + negative + phrasal verb + prepositional phrase
explanation: 'Show up' significa llegar o aparecer en un evento.

sentence: She turned down the job offer politely
explanation: 'Turn down' significa rechazar algo. Es separable: 'turned the job offer down' también es correcto.

sentence: The teacher pointed out several mistakes in my essay
hint: Subject + phrasal verb + object + prepositional phrase
explanation: 'Point out' significa señalar algo. Es separable: 'pointed several mistakes out' también es correcto.
